5 years of going nowhere.
From ₹1,171 in late 2021 to ₹1,155 today (Nov 2026) - a negative return of ~1.4% over 5 years. Even on a 3 year basis, returns sit around a sluggish 7% CAGR with zero real compounding.
Everyone calls this internet classifieds giant a new age compounder & a safe tech proxy. Yet if you held it for half a decade, you rode a rollercoaster from ₹1,171 down to ₹700, up to ₹1,800 & right back below where you started.
Look check its numbers:

🚫Expensive on every metric: Trading at 45.2x P/E & 91x Price to Free Cash Flow while the industry median P/E sits at 15.6x. You are paying bubble prices for a mature job portal.
🚫Paper profits: TTM net profit looks huge at ₹2,212 cr, until you notice ₹1,472 cr of that is just Other Income from startup valuations & treasury. The core business makes less than half of what the headline shows.
🚫Terrible return on capital: Even with zero debt & 38% operating margins, ROE is stuck at 2.45% & ROCE is 3.45%. Over ₹46,000 cr of reserves sit locked in investments that barely earn anything for regular shareholders.
🚫Growth is cooling off: 5 year sales growth looked strong at 24%, but 3 year & trailing 12 month growth have dropped to 12 to 13%.

Great business, terrible stock returns. Never confuse a famous brand with a good entry price, otherwise your money is doing nothing but funding someone else's exit.

Probujeni mediji in levičarski politiki so širili lažno pripoved, da Nayib Bukele zlorablja človekove pravice kriminalcev v Salvadorju.

Nerodno jih je bilo gledati, kako so bruhali o svojem duševnem zdravju in travmah, medtem ko so izražali sočutje do gangsterjev in ničesar ne rekli za nedolžne ljudi, ki so jih ti gangsterji umorili, posilili in terorizirali.

Pisali so dolge članke o ubogih kriminalcih. Jokali so zaradi zaporniških razmer. Nikoli niso jokali zaradi žrtev.

Izkazalo se je, da so logični ljudje radi, da so kriminalci postavljeni na pravo mesto, in ljudje po vsem svetu si to želijo tudi.

Haitijci so protestirali za Bukeleja. Ljudje v Ekvadorju si želijo Bukeleja. Ljudje na Jamajki si želijo Bukeleja. Ljudje v Južni Afriki si želijo Bukeleja.

Ves svet je opazoval, kako se je Salvador iz prestolnice umorov na svetu spremenil v eno najvarnejših držav v Ameriki, in rekel, naj to storijo tudi tukaj.

Zapiranje kriminalcev ni nehumano. Ni slabo. Ni kruto. To je najboljši način za služenje pravičnosti, varnosti ter ohranjanje miru in reda.

Gangster, ki posili 12-letnico, si ne zasluži sočutja. Gangster, ki zažge avtobus, poln ljudi, si ne zasluži svetovanja za travme. Gangster, ki izsiljuje uličnega prodajalca za njegov zadnji dolar, si ne zasluži odvetnika za človekove pravice iz New Yorka. Zasluži si celico. Zasluži si zapor. Zasluži si, da ga odstranijo iz družbe, da lahko družba živi.

Probujeni levičarji so to razumeli narobe. Ščitijo zločinca in zapustijo žrtev. Bolj jim je mar za udobje morilca kot za varnost matere, ki pelje otroka v šolo. Bolj jim je mar za duševno zdravje gangsterja kot za duševno zdravje dekleta, ki jo je ta gangster posilil. To ni sočutje. To je bolezen. To je moralna gniloba, preoblečena v aktivizem.

Bukele je razumel, kar razumejo normalni ljudje. Mir ne pride iz pogajanj z zlom. Mir ne pride iz objema gangsterja. Mir pride iz zaklepanja zla in odmetavanja ključa. Mir pride iz tega, da so ulice varne za nedolžne, ne pa udobne za krive.

Nihče se pri tem ne postavi na stran probujenih. Ne na Haitiju. Ne v Salvadorju. Ne nikjer, kjer živijo normalni ljudje. Ljudje so izbrali. Izbrali so Bukele. Izbrali so varnost. Izbrali so red. Izbrali so življenje pred vladavino tolp.

Izgubili so mediji, ki so se prebujali. Izgubili so levičarski politiki. Izgubili so simpatizerji tolp. In ljudje so zmagali.

The market does not reward a company for spending money. It rewards it for return on capital employed.
When a company announces a massive plant expansion, retail investors cheer because they assume big growth is coming. But look at the math. If a business worth ₹300 crore announces a ₹200 crore factory expansion mostly funded by fresh bank debt, they are taking an outsized financial risk.
If demand softens or construction gets delayed by six months, interest payments pile up, machinery sits idle, and cash flow breaks down completely.
Always check how growth is being financed. If internal cash flows are funding the expansion step by step, it is sustainable. If heavy debt is funding it while return on capital remains low, the promoter is simply risking the entire balance sheet on unproven demand.

🧪 Chemicals, Q2 FY27: बिक्री सबसे तेज़, पर margin सबसे ज़्यादा फिसला

chemicals की बिक्री तेज़ बढ़ी। पर लागत और China की वजह से कमाई का हिसाब बिगड़ गया।

Sector की तस्वीर (101 listed companies, Jul-Sep 2026):
• Revenue ₹68,775 cr से ₹90,436 cr, यानी +31.5% YoY
• Operating margin Q1 के 18.0% से 14.7%
• Net profit Q1 से −16%

यानी हर ₹100 की बिक्री पर operating कमाई ~₹18 से घटकर ~₹15।

🤔 Margin क्यों गिरा?
• Crude $100 के ऊपर, rupee ~₹94/$। Chemicals का ज़्यादातर raw material crude से बनता है या import होता है
• China में ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा capacity, वहाँ से सस्ता माल। SRF ने ख़ुद specialty chemicals में "oversupply from China" की बात कही
• Freight महँगा

उदाहरण:
• SRF: revenue +35%, profit YoY +31%, पर EBITDA margin 330 bps नीचे, और profit Q1 से −33%
• BASF India: revenue +24%, margin सिर्फ़ 1.9%
• Atul, Vinati Organics: बिक्री बढ़ी, profit घटा
• Tata Chemicals: soda ash में नुक़सान और गहरा

✨ फिर भी कुछ चमके
1️⃣ Fluorine chemistry
Refrigerant gas के दाम firm। Navin Fluorine (+57%, margin 34%), Gujarat Fluorochemicals (+46%)
2️⃣ Defence explosives
Solar Industries: revenue +69%, profit ~+80% YoY। Defence अब बिक्री का 29%, management FY27 guidance से आगे निकलने की उम्मीद में
3️⃣ Specialty में चुनिंदा नाम
Deepak Nitrite +62%, Aarti Industries +75%, Himadri Speciality +58%

ये तीनों segment पहले बिक्री, फिर margin दोनों बचा पाए। बाक़ी में बिक्री बढ़ी, margin घटा।

📊 Segment-wise
• Specialty (55 cos): +34%, margin 18.0% → 14.7%
• Commodity (23 cos): +24%, margin 18.9% → 14.3%, profit Q1 से −28%
• Explosives: +70%, margin 27% पर टिका
• Industrial gases: +16%, margin ~28% पर टिका

ध्यान रखें: profit की तुलना Q1 से है। YoY देखें तो एक independent review में 81 specialty chemical companies में से 63 का profit बढ़ा। SRF और Pidilite का Q1 असामान्य रूप से मज़बूत था, और Pidilite का Q2 monsoon की वजह से हर साल हल्का रहता है।

🔭 आगे क्या?
• China की pricing सबसे बड़ा ख़तरा
• Crude ठंडा पड़ा तो लागत राहत देगी
• नए plants लग रहे हैं (SRF, Navin)। पहले depreciation आएगा, मुनाफ़ा बाद में
• Fluorine, defence और लंबे contract वाले agro/pharma intermediates मज़बूत दिखते हैं

सीख: Chemicals में revenue growth से ज़्यादा ज़रूरी है spread, यानी बेचने के दाम और raw material की लागत का फ़र्क़। इस quarter वो spread सिकुड़ा।

देखने वाली बातें: अगले दो quarter का gross margin, China के export prices, refrigerant prices, defence orders, soda ash prices।

Journey in Numbers: HDFC Bank

HDFC Bank was incorporated in 1994 in the first wave of private banking licences after liberalisation. In FY26 it earned ₹74,671 crore, its balance sheet crossed ₹43 lakh crore, and it remains India's largest private bank.

Here's how it got there, year by year.

1994: Incorporated in August as a subsidiary of HDFC Ltd, with Aditya Puri, hired from Citibank, as its first chief executive.

1995: Opens for business in January and lists on Indian exchanges.

2000: Merges with Times Bank, the first merger of two private banks in India.

2001: Lists American Depositary Shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

2008: On 25 February its board agrees to acquire Centurion Bank of Punjab for about ₹9,520 crore in stock, then the largest merger in Indian banking.

2015: FY15 (year to March 2015) consolidated profit is ₹10,703 crore.

2019: FY19 consolidated profit is ₹22,446 crore, more than double FY15.

2020: On 26 October, Aditya Puri retires after 26 years and Sashidhar Jagdishan takes over. In December the RBI bars the bank from new digital launches and issuing credit cards after repeated outages.

2022: The RBI lifts the curbs in March. On 4 April the bank and HDFC Ltd announce their merger.

2023: The merger takes effect on 1 July, with HDFC Ltd shareholders receiving 42 bank shares for every 25 held, a roughly ₹40 lakh crore deal, the largest in Indian corporate history.

2024: FY24, the first year with HDFC Ltd on the books, brings consolidated profit of ₹65,446 crore.

2025: FY25 consolidated profit is ₹73,440 crore. On 19 July it announces its first ever bonus issue, one share for every one held, with a 27 August record date, and a ₹5 special dividend.

2026: FY26 standalone profit rises 11% to ₹74,671 crore, with total dividends of ₹15.50 a share. April to June 2026 profit rises 5% to ₹19,060 crore, and the balance sheet approaches ₹44 lakh crore.

Venus Pipes & Tubes Ltd – Q2 & H1FY27 | Concall Insights

Financial Performance
•Q2 revenue ₹361.1 Cr (+23.9% YoY); EBITDA ₹51.7 Cr (+9.1%); PAT ₹26 Cr.
•EBITDA margin declined to 14.3% from 16.3%, impacted by higher export freight, fuel costs and selling-price inflation.
•Exports reached a record ₹147 Cr, contributing 41% of Q2 revenue.

Revenue Growth & Volume Guidance
•Management targets ~15% pipe volume growth in FY27, against ~7–8% achieved in H1.
•H2 expected to accelerate through higher seamless/welded utilization and initial contributions from fittings and spooling.
•Export demand remains strong, particularly from the US, with exports contributing ~40% of the pipe order book.

Order Book & Revenue Visibility
•Outstanding order book ₹670 Cr, including ~₹640 Cr pipes and ₹29 Cr data-center spooling.
•Order book executable over approximately 4–5 months, providing strong near-term visibility.
•Additional ~₹155 Cr data-center LOI awaiting conversion into firm orders.
•Demand opportunities emerging from power, oil & gas, semiconductors, solar and CNG infrastructure.

Data-Center Spooling – Major Earnings Driver
•Management targets ~₹70 Cr revenue from data-center spooling in H2 FY27, with expected EBITDA margins exceeding 30%.
•Existing and upcoming capacity can potentially support ₹250–300 Cr annual revenue at scale.
•Additional spooling capacity expected to become operational around January–February 2027.
•Expansion planned sequentially into power, oil & gas and nuclear applications, subject to customer approvals.

Fittings – High-Margin Growth Opportunity
•Management targets ₹40–50 Cr fittings revenue in H2 FY27, versus ~₹9 Cr in H1.
•Expected EBITDA margins of 18–20%, improving consolidated product mix.
•At full utilization, fittings facility has ₹180–200 Cr annual revenue potential.

Capacity Utilization & Margins
•Seamless utilization currently 80%+, targeted to exceed 90% in H2; welded utilization expected to improve towards 65–70%.
•Pipe EBITDA realization declined from ~₹64/kg to ₹62/kg due to freight and operating costs.
•Management expects pipe margins to recover towards previous levels as freight normalizes and new orders reflect higher costs.
•Higher-margin spooling and fittings expected to drive stronger EBITDA and PAT growth than the core pipe business.

Debt Reduction & CapEx
•Raised ₹372 Cr through preferential allotment, with ~₹344 Cr earmarked for debt repayment.
•Expected annual interest savings of ₹28–30 Cr, benefiting PAT from H2 FY27.
•FY27 CapEx expected around ₹130–140 Cr, including seamless, fittings, spooling and solar investments.

Key Takeaway
•Strong H2 earnings growth visibility from accelerating pipe volumes, ₹70 Cr data-center spooling revenue, ₹40–50 Cr fittings revenue and substantial interest savings.
•Major triggers: Conversion of the remaining data-center LOI, spooling capacity expansion, pipe margin recovery and higher seamless utilization.
•Key monitorables: Export freight volatility, customer approvals, LOI conversion, working capital and timely capacity ramp-up.

🏦 India's Private Banks: HDFC vs ICICI vs Axis vs Kotak vs Federal Bank

Q2 FY27 results are out!

One bank delivered 45% profit growth. Another generated nearly ₹20,000 Cr in quarterly profit. One has the highest NIM, while another has the lowest NNPA.

Which is the best banking stock?

Let's compare. 👇

1/ Q2 FY27: Financial Performance

(All figures ₹ crore; standalone)

🔹 HDFC Bank
• NII: ₹34,620 Cr (+9.7%)
• PAT: ₹19,510 Cr (+4.7%)
• NIM: 3.32%
🔹 ICICI Bank
• NII: ₹25,339 Cr (+17.7%)
• PAT: ₹14,843 Cr (+20.1%)
• NIM: 4.18%
🔹 Axis Bank
• NII: ₹15,371 Cr (+11.8%)
• PAT: ₹7,003 Cr (+37.6%)
• NIM: 3.36%
🔹 Kotak Mahindra Bank
• NII: ₹8,459 Cr (+16%)
• PAT: ₹4,212 Cr (+29%)
• NIM: 4.31%
🔹 Federal Bank
• NII: ₹3,153 Cr (+26.4%)
• PAT: ₹1,386 Cr (+45.1%)
• NIM: 3.32%

2/ The Biggest Surprise: Federal Bank!

Federal Bank delivered:
• 45.1% PAT growth
• 26.4% NII growth
• 31.9% fee income growth
• Record quarterly PAT of ₹1,386 Cr
More importantly, growth is coming from its core banking franchise.

This deserves attention, particularly because Federal is operating on a much smaller base.

3/ Profitability: Who Has the Strongest Margins?

NIM comparison:
🥇 Kotak: 4.31%
🥈 ICICI: 4.18%
🥉 Axis: 3.36%
4️⃣ HDFC: 3.32%
5️⃣ Federal: 3.32%

Kotak and ICICI have a clear advantage in NIM.
However, NIM alone does not determine profitability. Cost of funds, operating expenses, credit costs and fee income matter equally.

4/ Asset Quality: Who Has the Cleanest Loan Book?
GNPA / NNPA:

🔹 HDFC: 1.11% / 0.37%
🔹 ICICI: 1.20% / 0.30%
🔹 Axis: 1.16% / 0.35%
🔹 Kotak: 1.04% / 0.24%
🔹 Federal: 1.32% / 0.17%
Kotak has the lowest GNPA, while Federal has the lowest NNPA.
Federal's NNPA at 0.17% is particularly impressive and represents a decade-low level.

5/ Growth in Advances and Deposits

YoY growth:

• HDFC: Advances ~10.5%; deposits 18.8%
• ICICI: Advances 24.1% excluding FCNR(B); deposits 17% excluding FCNR(B)
• Axis: Advances 19% excluding specified FCNR(B) impact; deposits 17% on a comparable adjusted basis
• Kotak: Advances 19% adjusted for FCNR(B) and acquired portfolio; deposits 13% excluding FCNR(B)
• Federal: Advances 21.7%; deposits 18.6%
The adjusted numbers are important. Large FCNR(B) inflows can inflate headline balance-sheet growth.

6/ What Makes Each Bank Interesting?

🔹 HDFC Bank: Scale, distribution strength and deposit franchise. The challenge is accelerating earnings growth.
🔹 ICICI Bank: Strong combination of NII growth, profitability, asset quality and operating efficiency.

🔹 Axis Bank: Impressive profit growth and improving asset quality. NIM and credit-cost trends need monitoring.

🔹 Kotak Bank: Highest NIM, lowest GNPA and strong capital position. Improving ROE remains the key trigger.

🔹 Federal Bank: Fastest NII and PAT growth, improving ROA and decade-low NNPA. A potential earnings-compounding story.

7/ My Investment Takeaway 🎯

My current preference for further research:
🥇 ICICI Bank – Best all-round combination of growth, profitability and asset quality.
🥈 Federal Bank – Strongest earnings momentum and an interesting smaller-base growth opportunity.
🥉 Axis Bank – Attractive combination of earnings growth and improving asset quality.
4️⃣ HDFC Bank – High-quality franchise, but earnings growth needs to accelerate.
5️⃣ Kotak Bank – Excellent margins and asset quality, but ROE improvement is important.

This is a research ranking, not a valuation-adjusted buy recommendation. Entry price and FY28 earnings expectations could change the order.

The big question:

If you had to own just ONE private-sector bank for the next 3–5 years, which would it be?

HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak or Federal?

🇺🇸🇮🇳アマゾン、インド再エネに2030年までに70億ドル追加投資
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
米ネット通販・クラウド大手のアマゾンは、2030年までにインドの再生可能エネルギーへ70億ドルを追加投資する計画を発表しました。
 
設備の建設が進めば、発電事業者の受注や電力供給の安定につながる可能性があります。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
📝ニュース要点
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
現地時間11月17日（日本時間11月17日）、アマゾンはインドの風力・太陽光発電に70億ドルを追加投資する計画を発表しました。
 
これは、すでに契約した40億ドルとは別の投資計画で、合わせると110億ドル規模になります。
 
同社は新たに4件、合計934メガワットの風力・太陽光発電案件も発表しました。
 
ただし、この4案件は追加の70億ドルではなく、既存の40億ドルの契約に含まれます。
 
内訳はカルナータカ州の風力234メガワットと風力・太陽光200メガワット、マディヤ・プラデーシュ州の太陽光300メガワット、ラジャスタン州の太陽光200メガワットです。
 
これらは発電事業者から電気を長期間購入する契約です。
 
稼働後、インドで確保する再生可能エネルギーの発電能力は2ギガワットを超え、350万世帯以上の年間電力使用量に相当する規模になります。
 
背景には、インドでの電力需要の増加があります。
 
新しい発電所はアマゾンの事業を支えるだけでなく、地域全体の電力供給を増やすことにもつながります。
 
アマゾンは、事業で使用する電力1単位当たりの二酸化炭素排出量を、2030年までに2019年比65％削減する世界目標も発表しました。
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

⚡主な影響セクター：⚡公益事業（再生可能エネルギー）
 
再生可能エネルギーへの投資拡大は、インドの発電事業者や設備関連企業の成長を支える可能性があります。
 
一方、アマゾンには電力を長期的に確保できる利点があるものの、投資負担も伴うため、オルカン全体への短期的な影響は限定的と考えられます。

Effwa Infra & Research H1 FY27 Concall Summary:

Profits grew strongly in H1, but cash flow went the wrong way. Revenue was up 44.8% and PAT up 48.8%. Operating cash flow was negative because of working capital, and the order book is still well short of the Rs 1,000 cr target for March 2027.

Key numbers:
• Revenue Rs 130.6 cr vs Rs 90.2 cr, up 44.8% YoY
• EBITDA Rs 21.2 cr, up 37.1%; margin 16.2%
• PAT Rs 15.1 cr, up 48.8%; PAT margin 11.6% (up 40 bps); EPS Rs 6.52 vs 4.38
• Order book Rs 675+ cr; bid pipeline Rs 2,400+ cr; new orders Rs 160+ cr in H1
• Operating cash flow -Rs 23.7 cr vs +Rs 23.5 cr in H1 FY26
• Receivables Rs 133.4 cr vs Rs 128.7 cr in March; borrowings Rs 69.5 cr; D/E 0.5x
• ROE 22.1%, ROCE 26.5%; private sector 44% of revenue vs 38% in FY26

Guidance:
• Order book of Rs 1,000 cr by March 2027; a couple of orders are in the last stage of negotiation
• About 80% of the Rs 675 cr order book can be executed across FY27-FY28
• H1/H2 revenue split of about 35:65, as in the past two years
• Rs 315 cr JSW project: 15-20% done in H1, another 30-40% expected in H2
• EBITDA margin of 16-17%; working capital at 180-190 days
• D/E to come back below 0.3x; growth to be funded from internal accruals unless they bid for single projects of Rs 800-1,000 cr
• ZMD final patent expected in about 12 months; the trial project under NDA also needs about a year

Key positives:
• The 48 MLD ZLD at SAIL Rourkela (contract value above Rs 200 cr) was delivered on time
• Provisional patent filed for zero material discharge (ZMD), which is meant to turn ZLD salt residue into byproducts that can be sold
• CRISIL raised its rating to BBB+/Stable (long term) and A2 (short term)
• O&M revenue up 60% to Rs 2.1 cr, and every major ZLD bid now includes O&M
• Bids placed for data center, desalination and CBG projects (including with EIL)

Key watchouts:
• Order book of Rs 675 cr vs a Rs 1,000 cr target, with about 4.5 months left. An analyst put FY27 inflow at Rs 55-60 cr, while management said Rs 160+ cr
• Negative operating cash flow came from payables falling to Rs 7.4 cr from Rs 25.9 cr and inventory rising to Rs 9 cr from Rs 0.3 cr
• 10-12% retention money stays in receivables for about 3 years
• An analyst said gross margin fell about 5 points; management blamed a higher share of supply work in the mix
• 20% of promoter shares are pledged to banks to secure working capital limits
• ZMD has no revenue yet: the patent and the client trial are both about a year away

Final view: Stable. Execution and profitability are on track, and ZMD gives the company a possible edge it doesn't have yet. But order inflow has to speed up, and cash conversion has to improve in H2, before the 2-3 year growth case gets stronger.

☀️ ALPEX SOLAR | Q2 & H1 FY27 Concall Takeaways

Management’s focus: integrated manufacturing, cell-led profitability and selective module sales as industry overcapacity pressures pricing. Key guidance & execution milestones 👇

1️⃣ 🎯 H2 REVENUE OUTLOOK
▪️ Management indicated ~₹1,200cr revenue for H2 FY27.
▪️ It cited ~4–4.5 months of selling visibility for the cell capacity.
▪️ Customer enquiries were described as strong, particularly for domestic-content products.
👀 The supplied summary does not quantify a confirmed order book or provide an unambiguous FY27 PAT target.

2️⃣ 🏭 TOPCon CELL PLANT: TRIALS STARTED
▪️ Trial production has begun, with the facility in ramp-up mode.
▪️ Management targets all three lines, totalling 2.2 GW annual capacity, becoming operational by month-end.
▪️ Utilities, gases and chemical systems were described as operational.
▪️ Further stabilization is expected after the lines start.
⚠️ Commissioning, stable production and full capacity utilization remain separate milestones.

3️⃣ 📋 DOMESTIC-CELL LISTING: APPROVALS PENDING
▪️ Management cited an inspection on the 24th–25th, followed by an expected listing process of ~6–7 days.
▪️ It indicated cells could initially be sold into non-DCR applications.
▪️ Approval could come in stages rather than covering the entire capacity immediately.
👀 Inspection completion and approved capacity will be important commercialization checkpoints.

4️⃣ 🟢 CELLS EXPECTED TO DRIVE NEAR-TERM PROFITS
▪️ Management indicated cell-level EBITDA margins of around 35%.
▪️ This is a cell-business expectation; it should not be applied to consolidated revenue.
▪️ It also mentioned 500–600 MW manufactured and sold in the near-term quarter, either as standalone cells or incorporated into modules.

⚠️ Volume timing needs clarification: 2.2 GW annual capacity equates to ~550 MW over a full quarter at nameplate output. The 500–600 MW indication needs reconciliation with commissioning continuing through month-end.

5️⃣ 🔴 MODULE PRICING REMAINS UNDER PRESSURE
▪️ Management described severe overcapacity and weak profitability in module manufacturing.
▪️ Alpex is deliberately rejecting non-remunerative orders, accepting a near-term revenue impact.
▪️ The priority is protecting profitability and returns while cell production ramps.
👀 The earnings recovery therefore depends heavily on cell execution, approvals and achievable selling margins.

6️⃣ 🖼️ FRAME MANUFACTURING: ANOTHER INTEGRATION LEVER
▪️ Alpex has been manufacturing frames for roughly two years and says expansion is underway.
▪️ Management expects BIS requirements and potential anti-dumping measures to support domestic frame manufacturers.
▪️ Existing manufacturing could provide supply security alongside an additional earnings opportunity.
⚠️ The anti-dumping investigation does not establish that duties have been imposed; timing and outcomes remain uncertain.

7️⃣ ⏸️ WAFER/INGOT PROJECT REMAINS PAUSED
▪️ Management described factory infrastructure as largely ready and financing arrangements as complete.
▪️ Chinese equipment-export and technology-transfer uncertainty is holding back further progress.
▪️ Restart depends on policy clarity; the supplied summary contains inconsistent decision timelines.
👀 No reliable restart date or updated numerical capex budget can be drawn from the commentary.

8️⃣ 💰 INVENTORY & FUNDING
▪️ Inventory increased alongside the second module facility, cell-input procurement and slower movement of finished modules.
▪️ Management cited stocking raw materials supporting over 200 MW of cell production.
▪️ Imported-input lead times could keep inventory elevated initially.
▪️ It expects inventory to decline somewhat by March-end, rather than promising a complete unwind.

Management also expects warrant conversion by the March deadline, while stating project funding is not dependent on those proceeds. Conversion remains prospective.

9️⃣ 👀 NEXT EXECUTION CHECKPOINTS
▪️ Stabilization of the 2.2 GW cell facility.
▪️ Domestic-cell listing and approved capacity.
▪️ Actual cell dispatches and realized margins.
▪️ Conversion of demand visibility into firm orders.
▪️ Inventory reduction and cash conversion.
▪️ Frame-expansion progress and wafer-project clarity.

Five Great Thinkers Who Explored the Nature of Reality

Indian philosophy isn’t merely a collection of ancient beliefs; it is one of humanity's deepest explorations into consciousness, existence and the nature of reality.

From the non-dual vision of Adi Shankaracharya to the profound inquiry of Yajnavalkya, Indian philosophers challenged humanity to look beyond the material world and question the very nature of the Self.

⚜️Five remarkable thinkers shaped this intellectual heritage:

1. Adi Shankaracharya – Advaita Vedanta: Reality is ultimately non-dual. The individual Self (Atman) and Brahman are not separate.

2. Maharishi Yajnavalkya – Upanishadic Philosophy: Explored the nature of the Self, consciousness and ultimate knowledge.

3. Maharishi Patanjali – Yoga Philosophy: Revealed a disciplined path towards mastering the mind and attaining liberation.

4. Maharishi Kapila – Samkhya Philosophy: Explained existence through the distinction between consciousness (Purusha) and nature (Prakriti).

5. Ramanujacharya – Vishishtadvaita Vedanta: Taught that the individual Self and universe exist in an inseparable relationship with the Supreme Reality.

⚜️Their philosophies differ, yet they share a remarkable ambition: to understand who we are, what reality is, and what it means to be truly free.
Perhaps the greatest lesson of Indian philosophy is this:
Don’t simply accept reality as it appears. Question, contemplate, explore and discover.

Ancient wisdom. Timeless questions. Infinite possibilities.

👉H1 FY27 & Future Outlook :

💠Own panel demand will continue to be served from existing factories; aggressive selling to be done through cells

▫️Cell contribution: ~500–600 MW of cells expected to be produced and sold, as cells or in panels, over the next ~4–4.5 months
💠Cell EBITDA margin expected at ~35%
💠Average realisation of ~₹22 for TOPCon

▫️Blended margin: expected to be a little lower than earlier expectations as module margins stay under pressure; pressure expected to ease from April 2027
💠Cells to be the major profit contributor in the short run

▫️H1 FY27 revenue: ₹885.01 Cr (H1 FY26: ₹903.24 Cr)

💠PAT ₹60.06 Cr (H1 FY26: ₹94.95 Cr)

💠Q2 revenue was lower than Q1 as panels were not sold at a loss

▫️Module industry: capacity of ~225–250 GW vs demand of ~60–70 GW, with some imports still allowed
💠Standalone module makers are under the most stress; this scenario is expected to last another 3–4 months, followed by consolidation and closures
💠Orders expected to move towards integrated players

▫️FY28: ₹4,000 Cr revenue is possible
💠On that turnover, ₹500–600 Cr PAT (15–16% margin) is possible
💠Current margins (historically EBITDA 16–17%, PAT 8–9%) are expected to nearly double at both levels with cell operations

▫️Long term: only integrated players expected to thrive as the industry cleans up; module margin contribution to return after consolidation

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Order book: ~₹1,600–1,700 Cr, expected to rise after ALMM List II listing

▫️2.2 GW G12R TOPCon cell plant (Kosi Kotwan, Mathura):
💠Trial production started and now in ramp-up; complete line with utilities running
💠Line 1 completes around 18 November, line 2 about 6–7 days later, line 3 about 6–7 days after that, taking the full 2.2 GW to operational by 30 November
💠Built in 16–17 months; fully stable ~10 days after full capacity
💠Raw materials for >200 MW of cells already stocked
💠~80% of machinery from China, some from Taiwan; Taiwan, Korea or Germany are options for future expansion

▫️ALMM List II (cells) listing:
💠Fees paid and process completed; inspection by officials expected on 24–25 November
💠Listing expected within ~10–12 days of inspection
💠Capacity may be listed in parts (a later visit can follow within ~1 week); the factory is ~1.5 hours from the approving agency (NISE)
💠Cells can be sold as non-DCR before listing; DCR-compliant sales begin after listing
💠C&I demand, given a 6-month reprieve, comes under the cell requirement from 1 January 2027

▫️Ingot and wafer (5 GW by FY30; first phase production by June 2028):
💠Technology tie-up in place, factory almost ready, financial arrangements largely complete
💠Paused because of China's restrictions on technology and equipment transfer; Tata and Adani have also paused
💠Decision expected around 5–10 January 2027, once the Chinese policy is public
💠100 MW pilot plant targeted by end Q1 FY28
💠12–18 months to build; 5 GW of cells expected to be in place by FY30

▫️Aluminium frame (12,000 MT today):
💠Capacity expansion started, to double or triple
💠BIS now applicable on frames from December; anti-dumping investigation started, duty likely in 2–3 months
💠Frame is ~10–11% of panel cost; in-house supply insulates against disruption

▫️Module capacity: 2.4 GW operational; 3.6 GW module expansion paused, with leasing of capacity possible if needed

▫️Inventory: elevated due to the second (G12R) module factory, raw materials for the cell line and unsold finished goods
💠Expected to come down by 31 March 2027, though cell raw material inventory will keep rising in the short run

▫️Warrants: ~₹97 Cr pending, with the deadline around 20–23 March 2027
